note: Scripture source: Kulish (1905), the public-domain Ukrainian Bible language_seed.py names (ukr-kul), fetched as USFM from the ebible mirror (gracious-tech/fetch_collection, bibles/ukr_pan) via scripts/bible_mirror.py — all 66 books, 31,082 verses. Take Root was egress-blocked. Every mined span was sliced from that text by script, never typed; Kulish's nested ‟ was normalised to “ (punctuation only).

The English edition quotes the ESV and labels its citations '(…, ESV)'; the Ukrainian quotes Kulish, so the ESV label is dropped (as the sw/ar/hi editions do) — the reference stays as the author printed it. Translated from the fixture as it stands, which already carries this slug's six BODY_CORRECTIONS citation repairs.

Kulish numbering offsets hit in this book (the author's citation is kept, the right Kulish verse is quoted): Genesis 3 (AV 3:14/3:18 = Kulish 3:13/3:17), Job 1 (AV 1:10 = Kulish 1:9), Song of Solomon 1:4/1:6/7:10 (= Kulish 1:3/1:5/7:11), Ecclesiastes 5:9 (= 5:8).

Editorial cases for review (self_rendered on purpose, where Kulish's wording or text cannot carry Spurgeon's argument): Amos 2:13 (ch16 theme verse — Kulish 'I will press you' vs the ESV 'I am pressed under you' the sermon rests on; Kulish's own reading is quoted where Spurgeon offers it as the alternative translation), Isaiah 28:28 (ch17, Kulish lacks 'he will not ever be threshing it'), Zechariah 4:10 (ch11, 'day of small things'), Psalm 119:113 (ch02, 'vain thoughts'), Ephesians 1:6 (ch15, 'accepted in the Beloved'), Genesis 49:10 (ch18), Isaiah 1:24, Isaiah 44:22b, Genesis 16:13, Psalm 34:5 (first-person), Hebrews 12:6 (ch17 — the English wording is closer to 1 Cor 11:32).

Derived by measurement: a row is mined only when the translator reported the quotation verbatim AND a quoted segment (8+ chars) or a 20+ char run of that block is a byte substring of the cited Kulish verse window. Re-personed, adapted, joined-across-verses and single-word quotations are self_rendered. Unquoted echoes are not recorded. 393 mined, 69 self_rendered.
